Do the iPhone or Galaxy S matter anymore?

I'd have said no a couple months back. But after using some other brands and then going back to Samsung (Note 4, actually. Not Galaxy S line), I have to say there's a place for Samsung Galaxy phones. They push the boundaries and introduce a lot of interesting new features. Nevermind that a ton of features end up being pretty useless, the ones that go mainstream are pretty darned useful.

Fellow Note user and I love it, but there was nothing at all about TouchWiz that I found useful and I've since flashed to CyanogenMod nightlies to see how that's going. Apple has iOS if that's your cup of tea, but I haven't played with an Android distro yet that was so good out of the phone store that I'd want to keep that garbage on there. My next phone will probably be a Nexus since the newest ones seem pretty slick, unless Continuum pans out for WP10, in which case I'd consider it -- ironically WP felt like the most fluid system for the relatively small number of tasks I use a smartphone for (calls, texts, alarms, email, GPS navigation)...but the lack of apps was the reason I got rid of my WP8 device.

Lots of people hate on Touchwiz and I get their frustration. However, I just install a different launcher and I'm over it. Plus, I get to keep some of the great things about Touchwize.

  • built in file browser
  • split-windows
  • draggable mini-windows
  • floating keyboard
  • power saving and ultra power saving mode has saved me a couple of times
  • s-pen tools
  • competent music player - I couldn't believe how difficult it is to find a player that offered folders-as-playlist out of the box.
  • Knox. It's actually pretty useful for compartmentalizing away work stuff.

The great thing about Android, once you get past whatever silly limitations your hardware initially comes with when it comes to root, is that you can make it your own so that you like it. Of your list the only thing I care about is the power management and music player, and I have both of those in CM...but that's just it: we're different users who care about different things. :)

I'm gonna agree with supersecretgf - all you need is a 5 gallon bucket, and plate to go under it to catch water (if there isn't somewhere otherwise you could let it drain off) and a nail and hammer.

You want to use the hammer and nail to add some homes to the side of the bucket, about 2" from the bottom. That way it will drain, but only when there is a bunch of water. Fill it up with soil and get a cherry tomato plant. I like Super Sweet 100 and Chocolate Cherry varieties, because they taste great and once they start booking, you can go out every other day and get more (pretty much)! Eventually you will need to stake/support it, and if you wanna get frisky when you are filling up the dirt, you can add one whole raw egg to the bottom of the pot. It will slowly break down and fertilizer the soil (and won't stink cuz it's buried in dirt). Or you can buy a fertilizer, or not use any of you get the varieties of tomatoes I mentioned.

These two kinds of tomato are the kind I give to people when they are first starting out because the low level of effort vs. the amount of snacks you get can't be beat.

The same 5 gallon bucket thing works with green beans and peas too!

I hope this helps. At least if you can find lettuce and broccoli, you cooks maybe find onions and add these tomatoes and have a salad?

You can plant basil in the tomato buckets too :) although the basil will want less direct sun, and the tomato loves sun, so until the tomato is big enough to shade the basil doing let the basil get scorched!
